findings.evidence: The 'Accept' button is styled as a primary blue button while 'Reject' is a secondary button, making the business-preferred option (accepting cookies) more visually prominent than the user's likely desired action (rejecting).
findings.explanation: The cookie consent banner presents 'Accept' as the primary action with a more prominent blue button, while 'Reject' is a secondary button. This visual hierarchy makes it easier for users to accidentally accept cookies rather than reject them, which could obstruct the user's goal of canceling a subscription by adding an unnecessary step that is harder to complete correctly.
The countdown timer creates artificial urgency to pressure the user into accepting the retention offer before the cancellation can be completed.

findings.evidence: The 'Continue' button is styled as a prominent red button while 'Never mind, take me back' is a plain text link, drawing attention to the business-preferred action of continuing the cancellation process rather than the user's goal of canceling.
findings.explanation: The visual hierarchy makes the 'Continue' button appear as the primary action, which could mislead users into thinking they must continue the process rather than being able to easily reverse their decision.

findings.evidence: The page requires users to answer two questions ('To proceed, please confirm your decision' and 'What is the main reason you are leaving?') before they can proceed with cancellation, adding unnecessary steps to the cancellation process.
findings.explanation: Requiring users to complete a survey before allowing them to cancel their subscription adds friction and delays the cancellation process, which is a common obstruction pattern in subscription cancellation flows.

legal.title: Résiliation en trois clics
legal.summary: Since 1 June 2023 (loi n° 2022-1158), a contract that can be concluded online must be cancellable online through a free, easily accessible feature.

legal.title: Simple mechanism to stop recurring charges
legal.summary: The Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act requires online negative-option sellers to provide simple mechanisms to stop recurring charges. (The FTC's 2024 click-to-cancel rule was vacated in July 2025; ROSCA still applies.)

legal.title: California Automatic Renewal Law
legal.summary: Consumers who sign up online must be able to cancel online, without obstruction.

legal.title: Ban on deceptive interface design by online platforms
legal.summary: Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 forbids online platforms from designing interfaces that deceive or manipulate users, including giving more prominence to certain choices, repeatedly requesting a choice already made, and making termination harder than subscribing.

legal.title: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive
legal.summary: Prohibits misleading and aggressive commercial practices, including non-contractual barriers to terminating a contract.
